text:
Maria Chen: FYI finance asked for a clear buy-vs-lease scenario for the hosted API Q3 runway. need numbers by EOD friday.

Aj Patel: summary from forecasting: 95th percentile demand -> ~2.2M GPU hours for the quarter. baseline (50th) -> 1.4M. seasonal multiplier from last year ~1.6x in Nov-Dec but we see a secondary shoulder in Sept now.

Kevin Morales: vendor quote landed this morning: buy = $18,200/GPU (A100-class equivalent), 3yr support. lease = $2,150/GPU/month with 6mo min. lead time for buys ~12-14 weeks for delivery + racking. lease capacity can start in 2 weeks but limited in APAC.

Sophia Li: quick math: if we need 1200 steady GPUs average to hit baseline (1.4M hrs), buying CAPEX = 1200 * $18.2k = $21.84M. Leasing same steady = 1200 * $2.15k * 3 months = $7.74M for quarter. But peak handling requires burst.

Maria Chen: right — we should consider a blended approach. propose laddering: buy enough for 70% of baseline demand, reserve leases for burst windows. keeps capex down and gives short-term flexibility.

Aj Patel: ran a quick sim (attached inline):
```
Scenario A (buy-heavy): buy 900 GPUs + lease 300 during peak -> handles 95th but higher capex, lower opex over 3yrs
Scenario B (blend ladder): buy 600 GPUs + lease 600 burst (rotate 3mo blocks) -> lower capex, higher short-term lease cost, better for uncertainty
Scenario C (lease-first): lease 1200 steady + extra 400 burst -> fastest time-to-serve, worst unit economics
```

Kevin Morales: region notes: APAC lease availability is constrained. if we lean on leases for APAC peak, expect 10-15% premium and possible 1-2 week extra provisioning. EU and US are fine for short-term leases.

Sophia Li: ops concerns: warm-pool sizing and cold start impact. if burst uses leased nodes in a different region, KV cache cold starts reduce token throughput by ~6-9% until warmed. need to account in latency SLO slack.

Maria Chen: also factor in model routing fallback: we can route non-SLA traffic to quantized variants during peaks to lower GPU-hours by ~18%. that reduces required burst capacity.

Aj Patel: updated blended sim after routing optimizations:
```
Buy 700 GPUs + lease 400 burst -> 95th coverage with quantized fallback. Estimated incremental spend for leases (quarter) = ~$3.44M. Capex = 700 * $18.2k = ~$12.74M.
Net GPU hours covered = 2.25M (with 18% token reduction on fallback windows)
```

Kevin Morales: ask to procurement: can we get a 30-60 day pricing hold if we commit intent? vendors might hold price if we sign LOI. also ask about staged delivery discounts for >1000 units.

Sophia Li: cluster ops checklist if we proceed with laddering:
- increase warm-pool to 12% of active fleet (was 8%)
- pre-seed KV caches for common prefixes before peak windows (batch warm-up script)
- ensure cross-region network egress budget for fallback routing
- add canary policy for leased nodes (tighter health gating)

Maria Chen: risk notes for finance: buying increases depreciation and balance sheet assets; leasing hits opex but is more flexible. we should model both scenarios for 3yr TCO including maintenance and power.

Aj Patel: small sensitivity table I ran locally (key rows):
- 10% higher demand -> need +120 GPUs purchased or +300 leased-months
- APAC premium -> +$0.3M quarter on leases if heavy APAC burst use
- 1 week lead time variance on buys -> pushes us to use leases for initial months

Kevin Morales: short-term ask -> can eng-infra confirm cluster warm-pool can scale to 15% within 72 hours? currently automation requires manual approval for >10%.

Sophia Li: I can automate approval if procurement gives a whitelist of vendor node IDs. will need a small runbook update and one pager for oncall.

Maria Chen: action items: 
- @Kevin Morales: confirm warm-pool scaling constraint and estimate time to provision + runbook (due: 2245124000)
- @Aj Patel: finalize 3yr TCO comparison buy vs lease with APAC/EU/US splits (due: 2245124200)
- @Sophia Li: draft warm-pool automation + canary gating plan (due: 2245124300)
- @Maria Chen: coordinate LOI ask with procurement + finance to request 30-day price hold (due: 2245124600)

deploy-bot: Reminder: quarterly-capacity-doc draft created at https://redwoodinternal/notes/q3-capacity-laddering (auto).

Kevin Morales: noted. will ping procurement for staged delivery terms and confirm expected provisioning time.

Aj Patel: I'll drop the TCO spreadsheet link here once done. preliminary numbers look favorable for buy at >18 months usage horizon, otherwise blend.

Sophia Li: +1 on blend. operationally safer and easier to A/B test warm-pool behaviors.

Maria Chen: ok team — sync tomorrow 10am to lock final recommendation for finance. thanks. :thumbsup:
